customManagers.description: Fedora base image via endoflife.date instead of the docker registry: the fedora:<next> tag exists on the registry months before the release is stable, endoflife.date only lists a release once it actually shipped.

packageRules.description: The custom manager above owns fedora; without this the docker manager would still propose pre-release tags like fedora:45.
Patch and digest bumps are automerged. They land before the 02:00 release run, so they ship the same night.
GitHub Actions. Grouped, and chore(deps) rather than fix(deps): a bumped action does not change the shipped artifact, so it should not cut a release on its own.
Minors of the framework and of the runtime image are real upgrades of the thing we ship. They get a human.
Majors are never automerged. They land on the dependency dashboard and wait for a human.
